assumptions: Emergency, chamber, monitor, and observation-slit states can be controlled and repeated, but their practical construction is unconfirmed.
The planet source can remain concealed from the set and reflective surfaces until S01-B03.
Final fixtures, power, rigging, exposure, color values, glass treatment, and playback method require qualified department testing and approval.
lighting_philosophy: Begin with restrained mechanical emergency and chamber sources, keep the reflection dependent on credible room light, and reserve the strongest color-and-value separation for the blue-green planet during Argo's pause.

setups.environment_time_basis: Interior medical bay at scripted night; emergency and chamber systems are active while daylight and planet light remain absent.
setups.motivation: The bay's emergency system and chamber diagnostics provide the only opening illumination.
setups.direction: Carry the emergency pulse across the glass while a shallow top-side chamber source retains Ninel's eye and frost.
setups.quality: Restrained shaped ambience with a firmer periodic interruption and controlled glass highlights.
setups.color_intent: Low-saturation cold-neutral base with restrained emergency red; avoid horror-coded alternation.
setups.exposure_contrast: Retain eye, breath, frost, and diagnostic reflection while leaving the wider bay incomplete and preserving headroom for the planet.
control: Walk the dolly path for reflections and spill
Keep the pulse mechanically repeatable rather than synchronized to breath
Record approved source and frost states
continuity: Match frost, glass, chamber level, shadow direction, and pulse state into S01-SH002
safety: Qualified crew approve power, mounting, heat, access, glass treatment, pulse comfort, and performer clearance
setups.dramatic_purpose: Let the room supply evidence while Ninel's chosen breath creates the story change.

setups.environment_time_basis: The same interior and scripted moments later; the chamber is open, emergency state continues, and planet contribution remains withheld.
setups.motivation: Opening the chamber redirects its existing service light into the bay while the monitor only reflects established sources.
sources: controlled bay ambience and negative fill
setups.direction: Extend chamber light across Ninel's face and right hand while keeping the monitor a near-black secondary plane.
setups.quality: Controlled soft facial shaping with restrained specular definition on chamber edge and monitor.
setups.color_intent: Continue the cold-neutral chamber and subdued emergency-red relationship without introducing an anomaly color.
setups.exposure_contrast: Hold Ninel and the disputed reflection at readable but unequal values while keeping the observation slit concealed.
control: Prevent monitor and glass reflections from exposing crew
Lock practical states for hero, reflection, and clean passes
continuity: Carry the opening state from S01-SH001
Match Ninel's head, hand, monitor, and source states for S01-SH003
safety: Qualified crew approve chamber movement, pinch points, camera path, flags, cables, heat, and electrical work
setups.dramatic_purpose: Establish credible geography and make the reflection disagreement possible without lighting it as proof.

setups.environment_time_basis: The same scripted night and monitor-facing position; only the already established interior sources may form reflections.
setups.motivation: The black monitor receives only controlled reflections from the established chamber and emergency sources.
setups.direction: Preserve the seated eye-height reflection vector and enough oblique room light for the disputed face and edge spill.
setups.quality: Naturalistic reflected softness with no brightness jump, halo, or hard accent tied to the delay.
setups.color_intent: Match S01-L02; the anomaly introduces no new hue and the cleared monitor returns to near-black.
setups.exposure_contrast: Keep reflected eyes at the threshold of legibility and match density across hero, anomaly, and clean passes.
control: Lock monitor angle, surface, head mark, negative fill, and source state
Capture matched monitor and reflection passes without an effect-light cue
continuity: Match head angle, monitor reflectivity, chamber level, and pulse state from S01-SH002
safety: Keep monitor, flags, support, cables, and reflection controls clear of performer movement and egress
setups.dramatic_purpose: Offer fragile evidence using existing light so the monitor never gains objective authority.

setups.environment_time_basis: The same bay moments later as ship rotation reveals the blue-green planet through the observation slit for the first time.
setups.motivation: Ship rotation brings reflected blue-green planet light through the observation slit while established bay systems continue.
sources: motivated planet image in the slit
setups.direction: Grow the planet contribution from behind and slit-side as Ninel turns, while established chamber ambience keeps her face accessible.
setups.quality: Broad gradual planet ambience with a defined slit edge; keep the world contained rather than washing the bay.
setups.color_intent: Let blue-green separate gradually from the neutral base and reserve its fullest approved relationship for the final answer.
setups.exposure_contrast: Retain Ninel's eyes, readable bay blacks, slit containment, and planet detail in one frame without spending the reveal early.
control: Conceal planet image and spill until Argo's pause
Coordinate performer, camera, light, ship, planet, and dialogue cues
Walk the complete arc for reflections, flare, clearance, and changing contrast
continuity: Carry the chamber and emergency relationship forward
Planet reaches its final mark before the word failure
Match face, slit, source, and cue states for resets
safety: Qualified lighting, electrical, rigging, playback, camera, and safety personnel approve implementation and rehearse moving paths with clear stop communication
setups.dramatic_purpose: Let the world claim the frame's withheld space while Ninel remains the anchor of an enlarged uncertainty.
